NodeJSNpmSetup.keywords: nodejs, npm, package-manager, nvmrc, engines, module-system, esm, commonjs, node-builtins, lock-file, sandbox-registry, corp-registry
NodeJSNpmSetup.Mission:
Canonical rules for the Node.js runtime environment: package manager discipline, version alignment, module system, project layout.
Goal: every Node.js project has a reproducible, explicit runtime setup — correct version pinning, one package manager, one module system. Same `npm ci` on the same `.nvmrc` produces the same environment everywhere.
Scope is the Node.js runtime layer ONLY. Language tooling (TypeScript, linters, formatters) and application architecture live in separate directives layered on top.
**Base axiom:** one package manager, one module system, one Node version per project. All three committed as files, not assumed.

BeliefState.Axiom:
One package manager per project: **npm only**. Forbidden alongside npm: yarn, pnpm, bun. `package-lock.json` is the lock; all other lock files must be absent and gitignored.
Multiple managers produce conflicting lock files and non-deterministic installs. If `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, or `bun.lockb` exist in the repo → remove them; add to `.gitignore`.

`package-lock.json` always committed. `node_modules/` never committed.
`.nvmrc` + `package.json` + `package-lock.json` is the **reproducibility triad**. Without lock file, transitive deps re-resolve on every `npm install` → environment drift.
Usage split: `npm install` locally (may update lock when `package.json` changes); `npm ci` in any automated context (reads lock as law, never updates).
`.gitignore` MUST contain: `node_modules/`, `dist/`.

Dev-tool packages MUST be pinned to exact versions. `npm install --save-exact` for packages affecting the build pipeline.
A patch update to a build tool can silently change output. Exact pins guarantee the same tool version runs everywhere.
Rule: runtime deps (published with the package) may use ranges. Dev deps affecting build output MUST be exact.
Pattern: `"devDependencies": { "vite": "5.2.11" }`, not `"^5.2.0"` or `"~5.2"`.

Module system declared once and never mixed. Mixing `import` and `require` in the same project causes non-deterministic resolution and conditional-exports mismatches. Choose at init; set `"type": "module"` (ESM) or omit/`"commonjs"` (CJS) in `package.json`. Do NOT add `.mjs`/`.cjs` files without an explicit dual-package strategy.

All Node.js built-in module imports use the `node:` prefix.
`node:` prefix is unambiguous — cannot be shadowed by an npm package with the same name. Also signals intent: «this is a Node built-in, not a third-party dependency».
Pattern: `import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'`, not `from 'fs/promises'`.
Applies to all built-ins: `fs`, `path`, `http`, `crypto`, `events`, `stream`, `url`, `util`, `os`, `child_process`, `worker_threads`, `perf_hooks`, etc.

**The lock file decides the registry. A committed `package-lock.json` already records which registry every dependency resolved from — install with that registry, unchanged. Force the public registry only when no lock file exists yet.**
**Lock file present → install as-is, no registry override:** ```bash npm ci npm install ``` Changing the registry a lock resolved from means re-resolving that lock — a decision at infrastructure-scope-discovery scope, never something this role decides per invocation. `npm ci`/`npm install` read the registry the lock (and any committed `.npmrc`) already declares; do not prefix them with a different `npm_config_registry`.
**No lock file yet (fresh install, first dependency) → force the public registry:** ```bash npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ npm install npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ npm view ``` The problem this solves: operator's `~/.npmrc` typically points at a corporate registry/proxy reachable only from inside corp network; a sandboxed agent doesn't have access → `npm install` hangs on `ENOTFOUND` / `EAI_AGAIN` or fails. Forcing `registry.npmjs.org` inline — not by editing `~/.npmrc` — resolves the first lock against a registry the sandbox can actually reach.
Why inline prefix, not a config edit: bypasses corp `~/.npmrc` without modifying it (operator's local setup stays intact); no persistent state in shell env — nothing leaks between commands; self-documenting in logs — operator sees exactly which registry produced the lock; sandbox-friendly — no dependency on inherited env from launch context. Mechanism: npm config priority — CLI flags > `npm_config_*` env vars > project `.npmrc` > `~/.npmrc` > `/etc/npmrc` > defaults. POSIX `VAR=value command` makes the variable visible to the spawned process only.
**Incompatibility — the project genuinely needs a private corp package, and the public registry 403s on it:** this is not a registry choice to negotiate from inside the sandbox. Both directions are closed to the worker — corp registry is unreachable, public registry lacks the package — so there is no per-invocation flag that resolves it. Halt `H_BLOCKED` per `AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION` with the facts (package name, both registries' response, whether a lock already exists) for the operator to decide: resolve the lock in a full-network shell, or grant the sandbox explicit network access. Do not search for a registry, mirror, or proxy that might work around the 403 — that is exactly the improvisation `AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION` exists to stop.
**Forbidden:** overriding the registry on a command that already has a lock to read (`npm ci`/`npm install` against an existing `package-lock.json`); modifying operator's `~/.npmrc` (breaks operator's other work); committing project `.npmrc` with a corp registry URL; silent failure / partial install when a registry is unreachable (operator must see the explicit error).

Standard layout: - `src/` — source files (JS or TS). - `dist/` — build output; generated, not committed. - `cli/` — CLI entry points if project exposes a CLI. - `scripts/` — internal dev/build scripts, not shipped. - `tests/` or co-located `*.test.*` — test files.
Predictable layout reduces onboarding cost and enables tooling to infer build steps without configuration. Different layout allowed only when documented explicitly with stated reason.

**Every primary npm script MUST be one-shot — returns control deterministically. Watch / persistent / REPL modes live in separate `:watch` / `:dev` scripts.**
AI agents (and CI runners) invoke scripts and wait for exit. A script defaulting to watch (e.g., `vitest`, `tsc --watch`, `next dev`) hangs the session — output streams forever, no exit code, no continuation. Agent has no way to distinguish «still working» from «ready, waiting for changes». Most common cause of stuck infra-setup tasks.
| Script | Behavior | Used by | |---|---|---| | `test` | one-shot, exits | agents, CI, smoke tests | | `test:watch` | watch mode, persistent | human dev | | `lint` | one-shot, exits | agents, CI, pre-commit | | `lint:watch` | watch (rare) | human dev | | `build` | one-shot, exits | agents, CI | | `dev` | long-running dev server | human dev only | | `start` | long-running prod server | deployment runtime | | `start:check` | boot, smoke-ping, exit | agents (smoke-test deployment) |
**Forbidden in `package.json` scripts:** - `"test": "vitest"` (defaults to watch in TTY) — must be `"vitest run"`. - `"test": "jest --watch"` — watch by default; must be `"jest"`. - `"test": "node --test --watch"` — must be `"node --test"`. - Any primary script that doesn't terminate without manual interrupt.
For `dev`/`start`: inherently long-running; agents MUST NOT invoke directly during task-execution. Need server smoke-test → declare separate `:check` script that boots, pings, exits within timeout.
Verification: before declaring infra-setup DONE, run each primary script and confirm exit (any code) within reasonable time. Hang >2 minutes without progress = violation.

Before adding any dependency, verify three things: 1. **Node compatibility:** `npm view engines` — supports version in `.nvmrc`? 2. **Module system compatibility:** package ESM-only / CJS-only / dual? Matches project's `"type"`? 3. **Pinning discipline:** dev tool → `--save-exact`; runtime dep → range acceptable.
Skipping these introduces incompatibilities that surface as cryptic runtime errors, not install errors.

SetupSteps.Step: Create `.nvmrc`. **One line, exact semver** — e.g. `22.14.0`. Not `22`, `22.x`, or `lts/iron`. Ranges and aliases produce unpredictable resolution across machines and time. Content must match `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`. Commit this file.

Create or update `package.json`. Required fields: - `"type"`: `"module"` (ESM) or `"commonjs"` — choose one explicitly, never mix `import`/`require` within the project. - `"engines": { "node": ">=X.0.0 =22.0.0 <23.0.0"`. Misalignment is the primary cause of «works locally, fails in CI».

Create `.npmrc`. **Required**: `registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` (or operator-supplied registry URL — never infer silently; source from operator interactively if non-default). Commit this file. Auth tokens MUST NOT be committed — use environment variables or per-user `~/.npmrc`.
Ensure `.gitignore` contains: `node_modules/` and `dist/`. Without this `package-lock.json` becomes the only lock-file guarantee — `node_modules/` committed bloats the repo with platform binaries.

Install dependencies. No `package-lock.json` yet → in a sandboxed agent environment prefix the invocation with inline env-prefix: `npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ npm install`. A `package-lock.json` already exists → install as-is (`npm ci` / `npm install`), no registry override — the lock already fixes the registry. Dev tools that affect build output: `--save-exact`. Runtime deps: range acceptable. See AX_NPM_AGENT_SANDBOX_REGISTRY for full rationale.

Add primary scripts to `package.json`. Rules: (a) only add a script if the tool is in `devDependencies`; (b) every primary script MUST be one-shot — exits with code, no watch mode (see AX_AI_FIRST_SCRIPTS_ONE_SHOT). Watch variants live in separate `:watch`/`:dev` scripts. Conventional names: `build`, `test`, `lint`, `format`, `type-check`, `clean`.

Declare the seven mandatory script bricks (only among tools actually in the stack): `type-check`, `test`, `test:coverage`, `format`, `lint` (read-only, `lint` reaching `gennady`), plus `format:fix`, `lint:fix` — each MUST carry its tool's own write switch (`--write` / `--fix` / `--autofix`); a `*:fix` script with no such switch is a configuration error («a fixer that never mutates»). Task tickets and phase agents never call `check`/`fix`/any single brick by hand — they run `npx gennady sdd-verify --profile ` (the ladder tool), which calls the bricks itself. `check` and `fix` are two OPTIONAL wrapper scripts, for the human / CI / pre-commit path only: `"check": "npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full"`; `"fix": "npm run format:fix && npm run lint:fix"`. Declare `check-command → npm run check` and `fix-command → npm run fix` in infra-spec §Verification Commands as these human/CI wrappers — not as a per-ticket verification alias (ticket §5 rows write the `sdd-verify --profile ` call directly). Include only active phases among the seven bricks; all commands are one-shot.

Confirm three files committed: `.nvmrc`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (`npm ci` reads all three). Run HOOK_NVMRC_EXACT and HOOK_NPMRC_REGISTRY. Run each primary script — must exit within 2 minutes; hang = watch-mode violation.

Definitions.Definition: Three committed files guaranteeing reproducible Node.js environment: `.nvmrc` (Node version), `package.json` (declared deps), `package-lock.json` (resolved dep tree). `npm ci` reads all three.
A version string with no range operator: `5.2.11`, not `^5.2.0`, `~5.2`, or `5.x`.
ECMAScript Modules. Activated by `"type": "module"`. Syntax: `import`/`export`. Local imports require explicit extensions.
CommonJS. Default when `"type"` is absent or `"commonjs"`. Syntax: `require`/`module.exports`. Synchronous resolution.

Pattern.Intent: Minimal valid `package.json`: explicit module system, engines aligned, exact dev-tool pins.
Pattern.Why: `"type": "module"` makes ESM explicit. `engines` bounds Node version. `vite` exact-pinned (build tool); `some-lib` uses range (runtime dep).
Single exact version. `nvm use` resolves unambiguously. No range, no alias, no comments.
Registry explicit. Audit on by default. No auth tokens — those go in env vars or per-user `~/.npmrc`.

Pattern.Intent: ESM imports of Node built-ins with `node:` prefix and explicit local extensions.
Pattern.Why: `node:` prefix prevents shadowing. Explicit `.js` extensions required in ESM for Node to resolve local files correctly.

Pattern.Intent: Correct workflow for adding a new package.
Pattern.Snippet:
```bash # 1 — Node compatibility npm view express engines
# 2 — module system (look for "exports", "type") npm view express main exports
# 3 — install with correct pinning npm install express # runtime dep — range ok npm install --save-exact --save-dev vite # build tool — exact pin
# 4 — commit both files git add package.json package-lock.json ```
Pattern.Why: Verification before install prevents silent incompatibilities. Committing lock with package.json closes the reproducibility triad.

AntiPattern.WhyBad: Each manager resolves transitive deps differently. `npm ci` reads `package-lock.json`; developer running `yarn` writes `yarn.lock` with different versions. Builds diverge silently.
AntiPattern.Good: Only `package-lock.json` tracked. Foreign locks deleted + added to `.gitignore`.

AntiPattern.WhyBad: `.nvmrc` installs Node 22; `engines` rejects Node 22. npm warns; CI may enforce constraint and fail. Local dev and CI run on different Node versions.
`nvm use 22` resolves to whatever the latest 22.x is at install time — different on different machines and at different moments.
10–500 MB bloat. Platform-specific native binaries compiled on macOS won't run on Linux CI. PR diffs become unreadable.

AntiPattern.Bad: `package.json` has `"type": "module"`, but `src/loader.js` uses `const fs = require('fs'); module.exports = …`.
AntiPattern.WhyBad: `"type": "module"` makes all `.js` files ESM. Using `require` in ESM file throws `ReferenceError: require is not defined` at runtime.
AntiPattern.Good: ESM project: `import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'; export { load };`.

AntiPattern.WhyBad: A third-party package named `fs` or `path` would shadow the built-in silently. Intent ambiguous: built-in or dependency?
Semver-compatible update can silently change build output. CI installs 5.2.11 today, 5.2.12 next week — builds diverge.
Each developer and CI runner resolves from whatever registry their global `~/.npmrc` points to. Private-registry users silently fall back to public or fail with 404.

Hook.Command: node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if(!p.engines?.node) process.exit(1); console.log('engines.node:', p.engines.node)"
git ls-files node_modules | head -1 | grep -q . && echo "FAIL: node_modules tracked" || echo "OK"
for f in yarn.lock pnpm-lock.yaml bun.lockb; do test -f "$f" && echo "FAIL: $f present"; done; echo "OK"

Hook.Expected: Prints `module system: module` or `module system: commonjs (default)`.

NodeJSNpmSetup.RewardCriteria:
✅ `.nvmrc` exists, one line, exact semver. `package.json#engines.node` accepts the version in `.nvmrc`. ✅ Only `npm` used; `package-lock.json` committed; no foreign lock files. `node_modules/` gitignored. ✅ Module system declared once; not mixed. All Node built-in imports use `node:` prefix. ✅ Dev-tool packages exact-pinned. `.npmrc` committed with explicit `registry=` line. ✅ npm scripts call only tools in `devDependencies`. Primary scripts (`test`, `lint`, `build`, `type-check`) one-shot. ✅ The seven mandatory bricks (`type-check`, `test`, `test:coverage`, `format`, `lint`, `format:fix`, `lint:fix`) are declared among active phases; `format:fix`/`lint:fix` each carry a real write switch. `check`/`fix` — if declared — are the optional human/CI wrappers (`check` = `npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full`; `fix` = `format:fix && lint:fix`), `check-command`/`fix-command` declared in infra-spec §Verification Commands as such, never as the ticket's per-phase verification alias. ✅ Before adding a package: `engines` and module-system compatibility verified. ✅ Lock file present → install reads its registry as-is, no override. No lock yet → sandboxed agent forces the public registry via inline env-prefix. ✅ Registry incompatible with a required corp package on both sides → agent halts `[!] BLOCKED` with the facts, defers to the operator.
❌ `.nvmrc` missing / contains range / alias / multiple lines. ❌ `package.json#engines` absent or incompatible with `.nvmrc`. ❌ Foreign lock files present; `package-lock.json` missing or not committed. ❌ `node_modules/` committed or not in `.gitignore`. ❌ Module system mixed (`import` and `require` coexist in `.js`). ❌ Node built-in imported without `node:` prefix. ❌ Dev-tool pinned to range; `.npmrc` absent or no `registry=` line. ❌ npm script calls a tool not in `devDependencies`. ❌ Any of the seven mandatory bricks missing while its rule is active in scope. ❌ `format:fix` / `lint:fix` declared with no write switch (`--write`/`--fix`/`--autofix`) — a fixer that never mutates. ❌ Any brick sub-command defaults to watch / persistent mode — agent invocations hang indefinitely. ❌ A ticket §5 row aliases `check-command` instead of writing `npx gennady sdd-verify --profile ` directly. ❌ `npm install`/`npm ci` without env-prefix in sandbox when no lock file exists yet; overriding the registry on a command that already has a lock to read; modifying operator's `~/.npmrc`; committing project `.npmrc` with corp registry URL.
